profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at an environmental law firm and policy center preparing a joint legal-policy packet for a multijurisdictional river-basin workshop. The firm represents a coalition of irrigation districts and municipal water providers in a basin that crosses a state line and an international border. The meeting is between the litigation/regulatory workstream and the government-affairs/research workstream to align on interfaces before materials go to a partner university and outside counsel. The agenda is to confirm what goes into the 'basin memo,' which map set and authority table will be shared, how citations and legal caveats will be handled, and who will circulate the version sent out on Thursday. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, handoffs, and timing for a single coordinated packet.

members.name: Elena Ruiz
members.role: Senior Counsel, Water and Interstate Resources
members.expertise: Interstate compacts, federal reclamation law, transboundary water disputes, and legal risk review
members.background: Elena is a partner-track attorney who has spent a decade advising public water agencies on basin governance, including litigation-sensitive briefing for cross-border river management issues.
members.private_state: She wants the packet to be safe to circulate beyond the client team without creating discoverable overstatements, and she is trying to minimize last-minute substantive edits from outside counsel by keeping the legal framing tightly controlled.
hidden_assumptions: The 'basin memo' means a legally scrubbed external-facing memorandum that can be shared with partner institutions with only minor formatting changes.
The 'current map' refers to the annotated jurisdictional map set revised after last month's client comments, not the older hydrology-first research maps.
If a claim is described as 'cleared,' that means she has completed legal-risk review and citations are bluebook-ready enough for outside circulation.
The authority table covers only enforceable legal authorities and formal intergovernmental instruments, not soft-law practices or agency MOUs unless they affect legal obligations.

members.name: Marcus Lee
members.expertise: Interagency coordination, comparative water policy, stakeholder workshops, and translating research into government-facing briefings
members.background: Marcus previously worked at a regional water commission and now leads the policy workstream that assembles cross-border governance materials for workshops, legislative staff, and coalition partners.
members.private_state: He wants a substantively rich packet that demonstrates practical basin-wide coordination options, and he is trying to preserve the research team's framing before it gets narrowed into a purely litigation-oriented product.
hidden_assumptions: The 'basin memo' means the substantive workshop brief that synthesizes law, policy practice, and institutional gaps for discussion, even if formal legal caveats are added later.
The 'current map' refers to the latest GIS basin package in the shared drive, which foregrounds watershed continuity and agency overlap rather than litigation annotations.
If a section is 'cleared,' that means the content team has approved it for inclusion because the factual sourcing is stable, even if legal formatting and caveats are still pending.

The authority table should include operational agreements, binational minutes, agency coordination protocols, and recurring practices because those are what workshop participants will treat as governing arrangements.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the basin memo
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the basin memo' as the central deliverable for Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a concise external-facing legal memorandum focused on binding authorities, key jurisdictional constraints, and carefully hedged analysis.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a broader workshop brief combining legal background, governance practice, maps, and discussion-oriented framing for policy participants.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a coordination meeting, 'memo' is a natural umbrella term, and both expect annexes and edits anyway, so the difference in genre feels too obvious to mention.

misalignment_points.topic: Which map set is the current map
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to attach 'the current map' or 'latest map' to the packet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the redlined jurisdictional exhibit dated April 18 that labels compact boundaries, federal project service areas, and pending dispute zones for legal context.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the GIS export uploaded April 22 that shows sub-basins, cross-border infrastructure, and agency overlap for workshop discussion.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both map sets are recent, both sit in the same shared folder, and 'current' sounds like a harmless reference to recency rather than to a specific file lineage.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say certain sections will be 'cleared' before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes a section is cleared only once legal review is done, risk-sensitive wording is settled, and citations are in near-final external form.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes a section is cleared once the policy team agrees the substance is reliable and coherent enough to include in the packet for partner review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Teams often use 'cleared' as shorthand for readiness, and in cross-functional work it is easy for each side to assume its own readiness threshold is the shared default.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the packet needs an 'authority table' for the basin.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the table is limited to statutes, compact provisions, treaty elements, adjudications, and binding agency delegations that create legal authority.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the table also includes nonbinding but operationally important coordination instruments such as MOUs, binational commission minutes, drought contingency protocols, and recurring cross-agency practices.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: An authority table sounds like a routine shared artifact, and because both legal and policy actors routinely use the word 'authority' in adjacent ways, the boundary of inclusion remains unstated.
